resources.string: Watches only for the short-video feeds of the apps you choose, so it can pause them after a long scrolling session. It reads the structure of those screens to tell a Reels or Shorts feed apart from the rest of the app. It never reads text, captions or messages, and the app has no internet permission, so nothing it observes can leave your device.
Messages, search, and the rest of the app still work. So does every other app on your phone.\n\nPress home whenever you like — this screen will be waiting if you come back.
Short-video feeds get paused after a long scroll. Nothing else is limited.
Interruptor is watching the apps selected below.
Interruptor needs the accessibility permission to tell a short-video feed apart from the rest of an app.
Scroll a short-video feed for %1$d minutes and it pauses.
You get a %1$d second warning first.
That feed stays paused for %1$d minutes.
Time only counts while you are actually swiping — watching one long video does not count.
Only the short-video feed is paused. Messages and every other app keep working.

This app has no internet permission at all, so nothing it sees can be sent anywhere. It reads only the structure of the screen — never text, captions, or messages. Everything it stores stays on this device and is excluded from backups.
